problem.text: Suppose $r, s, t$ are the roots of the polynomial $x^3 - 2x + 3$. Find $$\frac{1}{r^3 - 2} + \frac{1}{s^3 - 2} + \frac{1}{t^3 - 2}$$

steps.title: Where to start: lower the cubes
steps.body: The denominators contain $r^3$, and $r$ is a root of $x^3 - 2x + 3$. Being a root means $r^3 - 2r + 3 = 0$, so $r^3$ can be replaced by something of degree $1$. The same works for $s$ and $t$.

steps.title: Combine the three fractions
steps.body: So we want $\frac{1}{2r-5} + \frac{1}{2s-5} + \frac{1}{2t-5}$. None of these denominators is $0$, because $x = \frac{5}{2}$ is not a root: $\frac{125}{8} - 5 + 3 \neq 0$. Over the common denominator $(2r-5)(2s-5)(2t-5)$, the numerator is the sum of the three products of two factors.

your_turn.prompt: Expand $(2s-5)(2t-5)$. Then, adding the three similar products, what is the numerator in terms of $r+s+t$ and $rs+rt+st$?
your_turn.answer: $(2s-5)(2t-5) = 4st - 10s - 10t + 25$. Each letter appears in two of the products, so the sum is $4(rs+rt+st) - 20(r+s+t) + 75$.

steps.title: Expand the denominator and get Vieta's values
steps.body:
Expanding the product of all three factors gives
$$(2r-5)(2s-5)(2t-5) = 8rst - 20(rs+rt+st) + 50(r+s+t) - 125$$
Careful: do not drop the constants $+75$ in the numerator and $-125$ here. Now Vieta's formulas for a cubic $x^3 + px^2 + qx + w$ give $r+s+t = -p$, $rs+rt+st = q$ and $rst = -w$.

steps.title: Put it together
steps.body: The numerator is $4(-2) - 20(0) + 75 = 67$. The denominator is $8(-3) - 20(-2) + 50(0) - 125 = -24 + 40 - 125 = -109$. So the sum is $\frac{67}{-109}$, and the answer is **$-\frac{67}{109}$**.
